references.text: The same ritual of releasing the live bird outside the city is also performed in the cleansing of a leper, as a symbol that impurity is carried away.
Describes the beginning of the cleansing ritual with two birds, where one is slaughtered and the other released, as a parallel to the cleansing of a house.
The scapegoat released into the wilderness on the Day of Atonement carries the people's sins away, in a similar way that the bird carries the house's impurity out to the open field.
The priest makes atonement and the leper is cleansed, the same atoning motive as in the cleansing of a house.
The context for the cleansing of a house, where the priest declares the house clean after the leprosy has gone, and the cleansing ritual begins.
Hebrews explains that almost everything is cleansed with blood according to the law, and without the shedding of blood there is no forgiveness - this principle underlies the cleansing ritual.
